I farm only 4.1 mu, so I count every bag and every watering. At my age I do not like to gamble with the field. I start from what has worked here in Quzhou before, then I adjust a little if the weather and price look different. On my land, wheat and maize are still the main stomach crops, and with well irrigation I will keep them steady first. I will put about 3 mu into the wheat-maize rotation and leave 1.1 mu for cotton. For seed, I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize, because around here those have shown stable yield, and I will keep cotton on a better-performing seed too. Fertilizer is expensive, but I would rather spend a bit more than watch the crop turn yellow and lose output. Wheat I will feed mainly with nitrogen and some phosphorus as base fertilizer, then add more nitrogen at jointing with one good irrigation. Maize I will give a heavier hand on nitrogen because if maize is hungry in summer, yield falls fast. Cotton I will not fertilize as hard as maize, but I will not let it go short on potash because cotton needs strength to hold bolls. Since I have well water, I will not depend only on rain: wheat about 2 times, maize about 2 times, cotton about 3 times if summer turns dry. Pesticide I will not spray blindly, but I will not save money there if insects or disease start building. On this small area I do most work myself, so I will keep tillage simple with rotary tillage for wheat and maize, and plough the cotton ground once to loosen it better. If the season is normal, I will aim for steady yield, not fancy yield.
